HTML file without a language
HTML files should specify the language of their text with the lang attribute on the <html> tag. Screen readers and text-to-speech engines use it to pronounce the text correctly.
Heading levels skipped

Headings should not skip levels, for example, an <h2> heading should be followed by a heading at most one level lower, that is an <h3>, not an <h4>. Screen readers allow navigating by headings and skipped levels make the structure of the text harder to follow.

Image without alternative text

Images should have alternative text, specified with the alt attribute, that describes them for readers who cannot see them, such as people using screen readers. For images that are purely decorative, use an empty alt attribute, like this: alt="". For SVG images, add a <title> element as the first child of the <svg> element, or for decorative SVG images, the attribute aria-hidden="true". The alternative text of all images, including SVG images, can be edited in one place with Tools->Accessibility.
In EPUB 3 books, the <package> element of the OPF should specify the default language of the book with the xml:lang attribute. Accessibility checkers such as Ace report books without it.
